title: Concerning why if a [Nail] is cut the Person shall not be sick; but if a Limb is cut he shall immediately be pained.
teaching_text:
Once again one of the disciples questioned the apostle. He says to him:

“Tell me, my master, why when limbs are cut from the body of the person he shall be pained? While if the hair on the head of the person's body should be shaved, and [the nai]ls o]f his hands and feet be cut, he does not notice it [...] Some of these even now shall grow an[d ...] again. Just as the na[ils ...] so the hair shall grow and [...] cut a finger, he in [...] on the limbs of the [bod]y that you [.. ⟨p.281⟩ ...] him [...] since this time to the [... ...] the body ag[a]in.

“So, [I besee/ch you], my maste[r], that you might instruct me of the m[atter] for [which I have ask]ed you.”

Then the a[postle] speaks to him:

“I am the one who will instruct you [about the less]on for which you have asked me! Happen you know th[at the] body is like the earth, wh[ile these] limbs als[o ...] of it are like the trees. There are varieties [...] of tree you shall find growing on the earth. They ar[is]e and grow again and stand firm. They have not [... ...] Again, there are others that if they are cut shall not [grow ...] and they grow, as they are li[ke ...] which shall be cut and grow [...] and [...] they too that occur [...] they shall be cut and not grow, resembling [... neither] grow nor shall they [... ...] it [sh]all please him on [...] and grows [...] in impurity [... ...] from him. This flesh that is corrupt [... ⟨p.282⟩ ...] in the liv[in]g flesh and they [... ...] are somewhat sick.

“Behold, [I have tau/ght you] about this lesson for which you have asked me [...]”

[... the] disciple heard this homily [...] he sat down.
gardner_synopsis: Mani compares the different responses of parts of the body to the growth patterns of tree varieties.
